summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a valid array-like length.
description: A whole number from `0` up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — the range a `length` property may hold.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a valid array-like length excluded from its type.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is a valid array-like length.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonLength(-1); // => -1
requireNonLength(1.5); // => 1.5
requireNonLength(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonLength(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
